subject: Post-call: VectorLytics POC success criteria, cost sensitivity & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@vectorlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: VectorLytics POC success criteria, cost sensitivity & next steps

Thanks for your time earlier, Oliver — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the POC: 

POC scope (proposal)
- Run a 4-week pilot against a representative VectorLytics query workload.
- Phases: 1) 2-week sandbox (integration + smoke), 2) 2-week evaluation window (metrics collection + QA).

Primary success criteria (candidate KPIs)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150 ms for 512-token prompts (production-like traffic pattern).
- Throughput: sustain >= 30 concurrent req/s at target latency (burst to 60 req/s tolerated).
- Cost sensitivity: target average cost/token <= $0.0015 under typical mix; flag if > $0.0025.
- Quality: pass rate >= 85% on the shared quality rubric (see attached eval_template_v2.xlsx).

Ownership & ops
- Redwood: runtime provisioning, model variant suggestions, observability dashboard + per-route cost breakdowns (Ben).
- VectorLytics: sample workload, data retention policy, and test account access (Oliver).
- CS lead: Marissa to run the evaluation cadence and daily check-ins during the evaluation window.

Immediate next steps
1) VectorLytics to provide sample workload and RPS profile by EOD Mon 4/26.
2) We’ll provision a sandbox and send credentials by Tue 4/27.
3) Schedule technical kickoff (30–45m) — propose Wed 4/28 10am PT.
4) Exchange security questionnaire (attached) and confirm retention/compliance expectations.

Attachments: vectorlytics_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC timeline + roles), eval_template_v2.xlsx (rubric + measurement examples), security_questionnaire_filled.pdf (Redwood answers).

Please confirm the KPIs above look reasonable or flag any thresholds you’d like adjusted — especially around cost/token sensitivity. If you’re good, we’ll lock the kickoff time and get the sandbox ready.

Thanks,
Ben

Appreciate the quick reply, Oliver. Short answers:

- Latency measurement: we’ll measure end-to-end server-side generation time (includes tokenization + model forward pass) and report p50/p95/p99. For the cost/token metric we’ll include only model generation tokens (not system prompt or embeddings unless you specifically call embedding endpoints). We’ll put a clear definition in the dashboard so it’s unambiguous.
- KV cache: default is ephemeral (per-request session) and not persisted to disk. If you need persisted caches for longer sessions we can discuss an ops pattern but it’s out of scope for sandbox.
- Data residency & retention: Redwood hosted runs in the US region by default; we record logs for 30 days for the trial and can export audit logs for your security review. We’ll add the evidence items you request in the security questionnaire response (attached).

Next actions I’ll take this week:
- Lock the kickoff for Wed 4/28 10am PT and send calendar invite.
- Provision sandbox credentials and share access to the eval dashboard by Tue 4/27.
- Marissa will send a proposed daily check-in cadence for the two-week evaluation window.

Thanks,
Ben

Oliver — Marissa here (CS). Quick note to finalize the evaluation cadence and acceptance gates so we have operational clarity: 

Evaluation cadence (during 2-week evaluation window)
- Daily 15m sync M-F for the first week, then M/W/F 15m for the second week. 
- Weekly written snapshot with the key metrics (latency p95, sustained rps, cost/token, quality pass rate).

Acceptance gates (final decision after 2-week evaluation window)
- Green: all KPIs meet thresholds and no unresolved security items -> recommended move to production pilot.
- Amber: one KPI marginally out (e.g., cost slightly above threshold) + mitigation plan accepted -> optional extension of evaluation for 1 week.
- Red: >1 KPI missed or security blockers unresolved -> pause and regroup on scope.

I’ve also added the HubSpot opportunity link to the related_links and included a short DocuSign template for the pilot statement of work if you want to fast-track contracting after a green readout. Please find the filled security questionnaire attached (security_questionnaire_filled.pdf) and the eval rubric (eval_template_v2.xlsx).

If that all looks good I’ll create the calendar series and the Ops checklist for the sandbox handoff.
